questions.text: The group chat: you send a message in your friend group chat. Everyone's online, but nobody replies for two hours. What goes through your mind?
options: They're probably busy, no big deal
I start re-reading my message five times
questions.note: Same situation, completely different reactions. The message didn't change, only the story we told ourselves about it.

questions.text: The result day: you get your marks and they're lower than you expected. What's the first thing you do?
options: Keep it to myself and avoid the topic
Shrug it off and move on
questions.note: Some of us reach out, some of us go quiet. Neither is wrong, but it's worth knowing which one you do.

questions.text: The bad day: you're having a really rough day and a friend asks, "Hey, you okay?" What do you most likely say?
options: I tell them what's actually going on
questions.note: Look at how many people picked 'I'm fine' or 'just tired.' Remember this the next time someone says it to you.

questions.text: The friend who's gone quiet: a friend who's usually talkative has been quiet and distant for a week. What do you do?
options: Wait for them to come to me
Ask a mutual friend if they know what's up
Try to cheer them up without bringing it up
questions.note: Most of us want to help, we just aren't sure how. Later we'll talk about how to start that conversation.

questions.text: When you're overwhelmed: assignments, exams, and family expectations all pile up at once. What's your go-to move?
options: Make a to-do list and power through
Sleep or scroll to escape for a while
Freeze and do nothing until the last minute
questions.note: If you picked D, look around, you've got company. Coping isn't one-size-fits-all.

questions.text: The comparison trap: you see a classmate post about landing a big internship. Honest first reaction?
options: Happy for them, but a little "what am I doing?"
questions.note: Two feelings can exist at the same time. Being happy for someone and worried about yourself doesn't make you a bad person.

questions.text: Saying no: your friends plan a night out, but you're exhausted and just want to stay in. What do you do?
options: Go anyway so I don't miss out
questions.note: Why is saying 'I'm tired, I need rest' so hard? That's worth thinking about.

questions.text: Who you'd talk to: if something was really bothering you, who would you most likely talk to first?
options: Nobody, I'd figure it out myself
questions.note: If a lot of hands went to C, that's exactly why sessions like this exist. You don't have to figure everything out alone.

questions.text: The compliment: someone gives you a genuine compliment. What do you do?
options: Say thank you and accept it
Feel awkward and change the subject
Wonder if they actually meant it
questions.note: Interesting how many of us find it easier to believe criticism than kindness.

questions.text: Asking for help: you're stuck on something and don't understand it, but everyone else seems to get it. What do you do?
options: Google it and hope for the best
questions.note: A lot of us choose D. And the funny thing is, half the people around you are probably doing the same.

questions.text: Your recharge button: after a draining week, what actually helps you feel better?
questions.note: There's no correct way to recharge. Knowing what works for you is part of taking care of yourself.

questions.text: The honest one: on a scale of energy, where are you right now, today?
questions.note: Thank you for being honest. Whatever you picked, it's okay. Let's make the rest of today a little lighter.
